figures.finding: Brunei has no rule of its own for child performers: no one may employ a child (under fifteen) save in a family-only industrial undertaking or, from fourteen, in light work suited to his capacity outside industry (a doctor's certificate decides); a person under sixteen cannot enter a contract of service, and from sixteen to eighteen only in an occupation the Commissioner of Labour approves.

value.from16to18: occupation approved by the Commissioner of Labour

sources.said: "child" means a person who has not attained the age of 15 years
No person shall employ a child in an industrial undertaking or in an undertaking which is not an industrial undertaking, except as provided for in subsections (2) and (3).
A child who has attained the age of 14 years may be employed in light work suited to his capacity in an undertaking which is not in industrial undertaking.

A person who has not attained the age of 16 years shall not be capable of entering into a contract of service. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other written law, a person who has attained the age of 16 years but who has not attained the age of 18 years shall be capable of entering into a contract of service in an occupation approved by the Commissioner
